newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stock ex head promises improvements.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stock ex head promises improvements.

text.p: The head of Argentina's Buenos Aires Stock Exchange said Wednesday his institution is improving to cater for the investment needs of private pension funds.

"The impact of the private pension funds is that the objectives of the Stock Exchange are not just to create more instruments, but to generate a good regulatory framework for institutional investors," said Julio Macchi, president of the Stock Exchange at the first convention of Argentina's private pension fund system.
"The challenge for the Exchange is to delineate the structure and the procedures to construct an adequate system for the funds' investments," he added.
He asked the funds to pay attention to the local capital markets as much as possible, rather than putting all their investments abroad.
He recommended changes to the current regulatory framework, including allowing the funds to invest in preferred stock and changes to the ratings of equities making more stocks accesible to the funds.
Also, he suggested changes to the trading charges incurred by the funds through their operations.
Argentina's private pension funds were established in the middle of 1994. They currently manage $4.2 billion in funds for five million members.
